# Environment drift checks

`docs/build/environment-parity.json` is the reviewed list of staging and production identities, required Edge Function and Worker secret names, and permitted environment-specific differences. Resource identities are public configuration; secret values are never loaded into the checker or report.

## Checks and release boundaries

- `pnpm environment:drift -- validate-staging|validate-production` fails before deployment when a project ref, Supabase URL, app origin, environment marker, Worker name, or archive bucket is cross-wired.
- Before deployment, the workflows validate that each required GitHub environment secret and variable is configured by emitting only its name when the Actions context resolves a non-empty value. Secret and variable values are never passed to the checker. After the staging deploy, `repo-staging` compares applied migration versions with the repository, a deterministic digest of live schema objects, generated TypeScript database types, deployed Edge Function slugs and `verify_jwt` settings, downloaded runtime source files, required Supabase secret names, and Worker settings/bindings against the repository and staging manifest. Provider version and bundle-hash metadata is included for diagnosis.
- The staging workflow uploads a redacted inventory snapshot only after it has gathered those facts. A failed gate fails the staging workflow and prevents production promotion.
- Production downloads the snapshot from that exact successful staging workflow run, deploys the same workflow-run commit, and runs `staging-production` before its smoke test. The pair check requires matching migrations, live schema digest, secret names, function inventory/auth/source-file digests, and Worker binding shape. It also checks each Worker's actual configuration against its own manifest entry.

The pair comparison permits only the differences named in `allowedDifferences`: project ref/URL, app origin and environment marker, the environment-qualified Worker service and archive bucket targets, provider deployment versions/timestamps and bundle hashes, and secret values (which are never read). Source-file digests remain strict, so a source change fails even when provider bundle metadata differs. Manifest and release-workflow checks validate each environment-specific value independently, so these exceptions do not permit staging resources to be wired into production.

Run the checker locally with the matching GitHub environment credential names in the process environment. For `repo-staging`, provide `STAGING_SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `STAGING_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF`, `STAGING_SUPABASE_URL`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`. For `staging-production`, provide production's corresponding Supabase access token and the Cloudflare inputs plus `STAGING_INVENTORY_PATH` to a successful staging workflow artifact. Never pass credentials on a command line or place them in a report. Set `DRIFT_REPORT_PATH` to save the JSON evidence artifact.

The report includes migration/schema/type digests, Edge Function slug/auth/version/source-hash metadata, GitHub and Supabase secret/variable names only, and Worker binding names plus hashes of plain-text config values. Runtime source file contents and secret values are not included. Function source comparison includes only runtime files reachable from deployed function entrypoints and excludes test-only files. A missing credential, malformed provider response, failed provider request, or unavailable artifact is a hard failure.

The checked-in `packages/db/src/database.types.ts` is the public-schema type snapshot. Regenerate it with the Supabase CLI against staging after a reviewed migration change, inspect and commit the generated type diff with that migration, and require the deployment gate to reproduce it exactly.
